title: Function templates
learningGoals: let the compiler pick the type

youtube.title: C++ Function Templates: One Function, Any Type | C++ Programming EP 69
youtube.description: In this episode you will write a function template, let the compiler pick the type and read a deduction error, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Function templates · 0:45 One function, many types · 1:25 From template to real functions · 1:55 Second program · 2:55 Recap · 3:25 Bug of the Day · 4:13 Challenge · 4:33 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "TEMPLATES" in tomato on lilac; Xecxec next to a cookie cutter that makes any shape; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a cookie cutter that makes any shape

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we write code that works for any type. With one template, you replace many copies of the same function.

scenes.onScreen: "Function templates": numbered lines (1. A template is a recipe for functions; 2. T stands for any type; 3. The compiler writes the real function for you) and an analogy card: a cookie cutter: one shape, any dough
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A function template is a recipe. You write it once with a placeholder type, usually called T. When you call it, the compiler writes a real function for the type you used. This is called instantiation. Think of a cookie cutter. One shape works with any dough.
points: A template is a recipe for functions
The compiler writes the real function for you

analogy.title: Function templates
analogy.body: A cookie cutter: one shape, any dough

scenes.onScreen: biggest.cpp: biggest works for int and for double
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 4] This line says that T is a placeholder for a type. [HL 5] The function takes two values of type T, and returns a T. [HL 6] It returns the bigger one. [HL 10] The compiler sees two ints. It makes a version with T equal to int. [HL 11] Then it sees two doubles, and makes a second version. The output is eight, and two point five.

scenes.onScreen: a flow: template, call, deduced type, generated function
scenes.animation: Steps drop in left to right with a pop; connecting arrows draw on; the active step glows butter
scenes.narration: Follow the steps. The template is the recipe. A call gives the types of the arguments. The compiler deduces T. Then it writes a real function, made for that type.

diagram.caption: a flow: template, call, deduced type, generated function

scenes.onScreen: explicit.cpp: explicit template arguments in angle brackets
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 10] We can name the type in angle brackets. Here T is double, so the three is converted to a double. The answer is four point five. [HL 11] Here T is string. Strings compare in alphabetical order. Pear comes after apple, so pear is bigger.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as explicit dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints four point five, and then pear.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A template is a recipe for functions. Two. T is a placeholder for a type. Three. The compiler deduces T from the arguments. Four. You can name the type in angle brackets. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A template is a recipe for functions.
T is a placeholder for a type.
The compiler deduces T from the arguments.
You can name the type in angle brackets.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: Two different types
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the g++ error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We call biggest with an int and a double. The compiler says no matching function for call to biggest with int and double. It must find one T for both. Name the type yourself, in angle brackets.

scenes.onScreen: I wrote a template for jokes. It works with any type of audience, but not always with the right one.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: I wrote a template for jokes. It works with any type of audience, but not always with the right one.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: write a template for a smaller value
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Write a function template called smallest. Test it with ints and with doubles. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: class templates. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

biggest.cpp: In function 'int main()':
biggest.cpp:10:20: error: no matching function for call to 'biggest(int, double)'
   10 |     cout << biggest(3, 4.5) << endl;
      |             ~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~
biggest.cpp:5:3: note: candidate: 'template<class T> T biggest(T, T)'
    5 | T biggest(T a, T b) {
bug.why: The compiler must find one T for both arguments. An int and a double give two different types, so deduction fails. Name the type yourself.

pun: "I wrote a template for jokes. It works with any type of audience, but not always with the right one."
challenge: Write a function template called smallest. Test it with ints and with doubles.
challengeAnswer: Write template typename T, then T smallest with two T parameters. Return a if a is less than b, otherwise b.
